Its current move is AI: the AI Visibility Stack guide anchored its 20 year announcement on 13 May 2026, and 18 of its 24 LinkedIn ads on record are staff thought leader ads on AI search. Its house contradicts two lines: no llms.txt while selling AI visibility, no Google ads of its own while selling paid search. A rival should know the book is brand first, 12 of its 25 clients are names only, and the local line has no LSA evidence.

openings:
Lead with the two observed contradictions: no llms.txt beside 14 AI topic URLs while selling AI visibility, and no Google ads of its own while selling paid search. The strongest judgment sits on local: it sells Local SEO to multilocation providers, yet the Horus read finds light local work and no LSA evidence (P3 absent) and the Local line scores 1, so it is likely, moderate confidence, that a rival treating LSAs and Sponsored Places as core healthcare local work takes the multilocation and dental accounts. Falsifier: an LSA or Sponsored Places case study appearing in the record.

Second, AI: the AI Visibility Stack is a framework and an ebook, P1 is partial, so a rival with a citation share scorecard for a named health system leads with the number; very likely buyers ask for it. Third, price: no public pricing and displacement 59.4 mean an offshore delivered rival can undercut the SEO and web hours, likely, low confidence. Fourth, brand and creative fills 11 client rows, so performance evidence is thin outside dermatology. Hard to beat: twenty years of healthcare only positioning and a 2,000 post blog; almost no chance a generalist outranks it on healthcare content.
